McCaffrey's supplied three-game receiving production is 28.7 yards per game, below 47.5, but this descriptive figure is not a projection or an estimated hit rate. Normalizing the supplied under -115 and over -114 gives approximately 50.10% for the under; that is only an offered-market comparison, not a Pinnacle benchmark or evidence of positive expected value. Nothing supplied clearly contradicts the limited receiving-yard hypothesis; keep it a lean without a quantified stake.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and the under lost because ATL led early, SF threw more than expected, and McCaffrey became the preferred short outlet. Eighteen targets over three games are enough involvement for one explosive catch to defeat this line, and ATL's 9.06 middle-field YPA allowance leaves an unresolved concern without route or coverage charting. Missing injury information could also conceal a redistribution of targets. These uncertainties prevent strong confidence; the base case and SF-leading flip support the under, but the ATL-leading flip does not reliably do so.
